ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB\parallel CD\parallel EF$, if $BF=3DF$, then what is the value of $\frac{AC}{CE}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $BF=3DF$,\\
it follows that $BD=2DF$,\\
due to $AB\parallel CD\parallel EF$,\\
it follows that $\frac{AC}{CE}=\frac{BD}{DF}$,\\
thus, $\frac{AC}{CE}=\frac{2DF}{DF}=\boxed{2}$

A left slanted transversal intersects them at A on the top line, C on the middle line, and E on the bottom line. A right slanted transversal intersects them at B on the top line, D on the middle line, and F on the bottom line. Reasoning: The problem states AB ∥ CD ∥ EF and BF = 3DF. Since D lies between B and F on the right transversal, BF = BD + DF. Therefore BD = BF - DF = 3DF - DF = 2DF. By the intercept theorem for three parallel lines cut by two transversals, the corresponding segments on the two transversals are proportional: AC/CE = BD/DF. Hence AC/CE = 2DF/DF = 2.
